TOKEN HEADER IS OUR CHOICE, NOT THE SPEC'S: the A2A specification defines PushNotificationConfig.token as a field but names NO HTTP header to carry it (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/topics/streaming-and-async/, fetched 2026-07-26). What is delivered is an A2A StreamResponse payload with an APPLICATION-SPECIFIC token header (X-A2A-Notification-Token) — it is NOT "spec-compliant push", and a foreign peer expecting a different header simply will not see the token. Every delivery proof in this case ran against a LOOPBACK sink this repo wrote; a loopback sink is not interop, so a foreign peer accepting these deliveries remains §6 leg 2 and `a2a` stays preview

D12 PARTIALLY CLOSED — OWNERSHIP VERIFICATION IS ABSENT: the contract names domain allowlisting, ownership verification AND an egress firewall. The allowlist (normalized whole-host equality) and the firewall (packages/egress + the pinned dialer, with redirects REVALIDATED per hop) are implemented and RED-proven; nothing verifies that the client registering a webhook target actually controls it. A deployment exposed to untrusted registrants must set PushPolicy.AllowedHosts — when it is empty the egress policy alone governs, and any public https host a client names will be POSTed to

DELIVERY IS NOT DURABLE AND NOT OBSERVER-DRIVEN: the pending set is IN-PROCESS, so a crash between accepting a notification and delivering it drops that notification — the retry/dead-letter discipline is the webhook pump's, but the queue behind it is not. Delivery fires only on the state-producing operations the server itself serves (message:send, message:stream, tasks:subscribe, tasks:cancel); there is NO asynchronous observer of run terminality, so a run that reaches a terminal state with no A2A request in flight notifies nobody. Both gaps need durable per-target delivery state and therefore a migration, which E19 excludes by construction

NO REAL WORKSPACE: every Slack proof this case COUNTS runs against a FAKE peer — a fixture that signs the way the verification page documents, a local HTTP server standing in for slack.com/api, and a fake WSS server built from the Socket Mode page. The shipped routes (events + interactivity), the Socket Mode connect loop, and the decision chain are exercised end to end over real Postgres, but nothing here is a receipt from a real workspace: no test that runs WITHOUT credentials opens a socket to slack.com. That receipt is §6 leg 1 and is what caps `slack` at preview — and Socket Mode is the cheapest way to collect it, since it needs no public URL

ONE SOCKET MODE CONNECTION, ONE WORKSPACE: the connect loop is proven with a SINGLE connection to the single workspace PALAI_SLACK_SOCKET_TEAM_ID names. Multi-workspace fan-out (N connections = N sockets) is NOT built — a listing query, per-connection supervision and add/remove on registration are connection-pool management, i.e. scale work. Two consequences a reader should not have to infer: a deployment serving several workspaces runs Socket Mode for at most one of them, and a workspace registered AFTER the control plane boots is not picked up until it restarts

AN ACKNOWLEDGED ENVELOPE WHOSE ADMISSION THEN FAILS IS LOST, and this is an asymmetry with the HTTP transport rather than a shared property: the HTTP route acknowledges AFTER the reservation commits, so a failure there earns a Slack redelivery. Socket Mode publishes no acknowledgement budget at all (the 3-second figure is documented for the HTTP callback and for interactivity, not for an envelope), so the loop answers FIRST — which satisfies any budget that may exist, at the cost that Slack will not redeliver an envelope it has seen acknowledged. A failing admission is therefore logged as a named loss and produces no run

NO RESPONSE PAYLOAD IS EVER SENT ON AN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: accepts_response_payload is decoded and slack.SocketAck refuses a payload on an envelope declaring false — the documented rule, enforced as a typed error rather than a silent drop — but nothing in-process has anything to say back inside an acknowledgement (an admitted run answers later, in the thread). The accepting branch is therefore exercised by the rule's own unit test, not by a real sender

THE APPROVAL MESSAGE IS NOT POSTED BY ANYTHING IN-PROCESS: the decision path REPAIRS the message a click arrived on (chat.update, bot token from bot_token_ref, per-channel Special-Tier pacing, one bounded 429 repair) and records its ts as the thread's repair handle. What posts an approval message with its two minted buttons in the first place is the credential-gated live leg (tests/live/slack) and, later, whatever composes approval UX — there is no in-process worker that fans approval messages out. Block Kit construction here is deliberately minimal (two buttons + the authoritative detail); a rich approval UI is the console's job. Enterprise Grid / org-wide install is out of scope: the interactivity route never resolves an enterprise id

NO FEEDBACK TO AN UNAUTHORIZED CLICKER: a refused decision answers Slack 200 with nothing done and is recorded control-plane-side only, so the clicking user sees no reply at all. Telling them would need an ephemeral message (response_url, whose 30-minute/5-use window is the wrong tool for approval repair, or chat.postEphemeral); that is deliberately not built

TERMINAL-SUMMARY MEASUREMENT: the proof's terminal_summary_posts counts the terminal SURFACE posts (exactly one repaired chat.update, never duplicated). The §63.3 fan-out form — one terminal summary per delivery id, with two canonical deliveries — is NOT asserted: there is no shipped Slack outbound worker to fan out, so a second post would be fixture theatre rather than evidence

JOURNEY STEP 8 IS COMMAND-ACCEPTANCE: the change_config route switch is asserted DURABLE (the row reads back queued on the session, carrying the new model), not APPLIED — applying a boundary config change needs a running engine, which this journey does not start, so that is an E08 execution-tier proof (apps/control-plane/internal/execution). Step 9's cancellation IS asserted to a real terminal: the §9.2 interrupt-delivery message reads back queued for the pump AND the run is driven to `canceled` through the production CancelRunReconciled path (§26.10/SES-010), with the run row re-read. A DEFECT this strengthening caught: the old step 9 posted Kind:"interrupt", which is not a command kind at all, so the coordinator durably REJECTED it on every run while the old assertion ("AcceptCommand returned no error") passed

EVERY PEER IS A LOOPBACK FIXTURE THIS REPO WROTE: the wired dispatch is proven against a fake A2A agent on loopback HTTP and against this repo's own T2 server. No foreign A2A implementation has ever answered one of these dispatches, so nothing here is evidence that a third-party agent would negotiate the card, accept the objective or return a reply this client can fold. That is §6 operator leg 2 and it is what keeps `a2a` at preview — the wiring moved the executor, it did not move the tier

THE PARENT IS FAKE-ENGINE DRIVEN (E08): the child.request that names the remote agent is a FIXED frame the test emits, not a delegation a real provider chose — no tool surface is opened to a real provider anywhere in this repo, so no live model has ever decided to delegate to a remote agent. The dispatch, admission gate and fold are real; the decision to delegate is fixture

A REMOTE CHILD HAS NO LOCAL RUN ROW, SO THE DISPATCH IS AT-LEAST-ONCE ACROSS A PARENT CRASH: the local paths fold a crashed-but-terminal child from its committed row, and a remote child has no such row to fold. A parent that dies after the remote completed and before the fold committed re-emits the same child.request and dispatches to the remote AGAIN — the peer may do the work twice. Closing this needs durable remote-child result state, i.e. exactly the run row a remote child deliberately does not have, and therefore a migration

THERE IS NO HTTP SURFACE THAT REGISTERS A REMOTE AGENT: a2a_remote_agents rows are written directly (the store's RegisterRemoteAgent has no route in front of it), so this path is reachable today only by an operator with database access. The wiring is real and tenant-scoped; the administration of it is not built

NO FILES SINK IS WIRED IN THE CONTROL PLANE: a remote that answers with a file part therefore FAILS its child rather than having the file ingested. That is the deliberate no-silent-drop posture, not file support — a remote child cannot return an artifact to this deployment at all

CANCEL DOES NOT PROPAGATE TO THE REMOTE (the remote half of SUB-005): a canceled parent cancels its non-terminal ChildRuns, but a remote child is not a run and the A2A client exposes no cancel call at all, so the remote task keeps working and its reply is simply never folded. Aborting our own HTTP request is not cancelling the remote's work, and this case does not claim it is

A REMOTE DELEGATION IS BOUNDED BY DEPTH AND FAN-OUT, NOT BY MONEY: the registered agent's max_cost_cents is stored and read by nothing — the spend happens inside the remote, where this process sees no cost and the reply reports none — and the parent's own token budget is untouched because a remote child spends none of our tokens. detach is also IGNORED on this branch: releasing a parent needs a durable job that wakes it, and a remote child has neither, so a frame asking for both runs synchronously

db_assertions: RELEASE-LEVEL entry, not a UAT case (it has no tests/uat/cases directory): a capability's maturity tier is not a behaviour one case asserts, it is the RECOMPUTATION over all of them

the verifier RECOMPUTES every tier from the canonical code tables + this bundle's own per-case outcomes and refuses any declared tier or /v1/capabilities snapshot that disagrees — the manifest's own tier copy is never an input (plan §T11)

PER-CASE STATUS IS AUTHORED DETERMINISTIC DATA, and what backs it is the CO-RUN in scripts/uat/extensions: the same invocation that verifies this bundle also runs the knowledge, worker and automation-queue component suites, the Slack/A2A package suites and the console playwright specs against the throwaway Postgres it stood up. A red backing suite fails the gate rather than being reported around it (proven by tests/uat/extensions TestARedBackingSuiteFailsTheGate); the shipped scripts/evidence/verify alone does NOT re-run them

HONEST CEILING — four capabilities cap at PREVIEW for ONE reason, that the counterpart system was never contacted: slack (no real workspace, §6 leg 1), a2a (no foreign peer, §6 leg 2), queues (no broker PRODUCT was ever run — the plan §T7 NATS-JetStream-container condition is UNMET and the durable proof is the Postgres reference adapter, §6 leg 5 EXTENDED) and console (every console proof ran against a FAKE /v1 upstream, never a real control plane, §6 leg 8). knowledge-vector and apple-build are DISABLED because no vector store and no Apple signing material exist anywhere. Only knowledge and capability-workers close STABLE

E19 WIRING RELEASE: this case's LOCAL seam is unchanged from extensions-0.1.0 — what changed is that the surface it exercises is now MOUNTED on the production path and its proof runs against the SHIPPED route. The counterparty is still a documented FAKE, so the case's §6 operator leg is untouched and its capability's tier does not move.

RELEASE-LEVEL entry, not a UAT case (it has no tests/uat/cases directory): a MOUNT is not a behaviour one case asserts, it is an observation over the whole RUNNING stack — E19 opened no UAT id, per plan §1

the verifier RE-DERIVES every surface's mount from the running stack's OWN /v1/capabilities snapshot and router surface, in BOTH directions: advertised-but-not-mounted is the §3.5 D14 defect verbatim (`capability-workers` was advertised `stable` by a binary that never imported the gateway package), and mounted-but-not-advertised is the same lie inverted

the mount observations and the transport-invariance counters were taken by apps/control-plane/internal/store TestWiringJourney, in the SAME process that served every route — a mount read out of a table would reproduce exactly the defect this anchor refuses

HONEST CEILING, the whole point of this release's NAME: it claims MOUNTED + CORRECT AGAINST THE PUBLISHED CONTRACT + READY TO RUN UNCHANGED, and it claims nothing about a real Slack workspace (§6 leg 1), a foreign A2A peer (§6 leg 2), a broker product (§6 leg 5) or a deployed console with a screen-reader pass (§6 leg 8). Every counterparty here is a documented FAKE and uat.WiringPeers makes that mechanical

NO TIER ADVANCES: uat.WiringPromoteGate recomputes this bundle's tier table and REFUSES any capability that sits higher than the committed extensions-0.1.0 baseline. Wiring makes a claim advertisABLE; only an operator leg makes it stable

contracts.requirement: discovery advertises only what is MOUNTED; a registration surface is what makes a `slack` mount reachable by an operator instead of by hand-written SQL

a delivery without a 2xx inside 3 seconds is retried three times (immediately, +1m, +5m); a non-200 answer carrying `x-slack-no-retry: 1` suppresses the retry, so a TERMINAL rejection must set it or a poison event is pulled four times
a retry carries both `x-slack-retry-num` (1..3) and `x-slack-retry-reason` (http_timeout, http_error, connection_failed, ssl_error, too_many_redirects, unknown_error)
event_id is globally unique across workspaces; that a RETRY repeats the same event_id is NOT stated on the page and is carried in the tree as a labelled ASSUMPTION the live leg asserts
the v0 base string is exactly 'v0:'+timestamp+':'+raw_body, HMAC-SHA256 hex, the header value 'v0='-prefixed, compared timing-safe, with a timestamp more than five minutes old refused

an interaction arrives application/x-www-form-urlencoded with the JSON in a single `payload` parameter and must be answered 200 within 3 seconds; the signature is verified over the RAW form body BEFORE `payload` is extracted
chat.postMessage is Special Tier — roughly one message per channel per second with short bursts — and a throttled call answers 429 with Retry-After in seconds

every envelope must be acknowledged so Slack knows whether to retry; NO ack-time budget and no retry count are published for Socket Mode (the 3-second rule is the HTTP page's), so the tree acknowledges BEFORE the work and names the gap rather than inventing an SLA

apps.connections.open returns a short-lived wss ticket URL; a `disconnect` with reason `warning` arrives ~10 seconds before close, and up to 10 concurrent connections are supported — so a graceful refresh OVERLAPS a new socket before draining the old one
the envelope carries `accepts_response_payload`; a response payload may only be returned on an envelope that accepts one
Socket Mode envelopes are NOT signed — the pre-authenticated WebSocket is the authentication — so the absence of a v0 verify on this transport is the documented behaviour, not an omission

the server POSTs a StreamResponse (task | message | statusUpdate | artifactUpdate), not a full Task; PushNotificationConfig.token exists for client-side validation but the spec names NO header to carry it, so our header choice cannot be called spec-compliant
a server SHOULD NOT blindly POST to any client-supplied URL: allowlist the domain, verify ownership, and put an egress firewall in front of it

the pushNotificationConfigs CRUD must mount on the SAME condition the card's pushNotifications flag reads, or a client registers a target against a card that says push is unsupported and is silently never fired
`queues` must derive from an actual mount; before E19 the queue store had no production caller at all while discovery advertised the capability as a static string
the terminal→enqueue half is committed inside the run's terminal transaction, so the outbound result survives a pump that is down — the delivery mechanism is never the durability mechanism

a hand-written fake upstream can DIVERGE from the real router (E17 T10's fixture invented an approval event the real approval.requested.v1 never carries), so the console's contract must be swept against the REAL /v1 mechanically rather than by review

live_legs.handover_row: §0.1 — App → Basic Information → App Credentials → Signing Secret
§0.1 — SLACK_TEAM_ID from the workspace admin page or any event payload's team_id; the Postgres URL comes from the running stack (make compose-up prints it)
§0.1 — App → OAuth & Permissions → Bot User OAuth Token (scope chat:write); SLACK_TEST_CHANNEL is a channel the bot was invited to
§0.1 — the signing secret, the bot token and the test channel together: this leg posts a real button and verifies the real click
§0.1 — App → Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate, scope connections:write. NO PUBLIC URL IS NEEDED for this leg
§0.1 — the app-level token and the team id, plus the running stack's Postgres URL
§0.1 — the bot token and a test channel, UNCHANGED from E19: E20 T1 asks for no new credential and no new scope (S3 — setStatus and the whole chat.*Stream family are chat:write)

§0.1/§0.3 — the bot token, a test channel, the team id, and a real user id for the stream's recipient (the approver allow-list's first entry; SLACK_TEST_USER_ID overrides). This leg answers S16(c): can a Socket-Mode-only app call the streaming Web API at all

§0.1/§0.3 — same four as above. This leg MEASURES S16(a) (what a never-stopped stream does) and deliberately leaves one open: it is exactly what a control-plane restart leaves behind, so the operator can judge whether the ceiling is worth migration 000042
§0.1 — the bot token and a test channel. This leg turns S9 into a receipt by making the recipient-less call our own client refuses to make

§0.2 — OPTIONAL: a foreign https receiver if the owner wants to measure the D11 token-header gap against a real peer. The deterministic loopback proof is complete without it, and a foreign PEER remains §6 leg 2
